$comment: POST /{page-id}/feed, read from Meta's Page Feed reference. Meta publishes no machine-readable spec for the Graph API, which is why this carries more prose than a Google provider: the documentation is the only source and it is prose.
title: Facebook Page post
description: Publish a post to a Facebook Page.
$idempotencyComment: The Graph API offers no idempotency key on this edge -- no header, no parameter. So it is honestly unsafe-to-replay with no way to make it safe: a retried durable run publishes a SECOND post to a real Page, and followers are notified twice. Deleting it afterwards does not un-notify them.

request.$pathComment: The Page id is a PATH SEGMENT. It is numeric and public -- it appears in the Page's own URL -- so unlike Telegram's token there is nothing sensitive about it being in a path a proxy logs.

config.label: Page ID
config.description: The numeric Page id. Find it under the Page's About section, or as the `id` on the /me/accounts response used to obtain the token.

config.label: Message
config.description: The post text. Required unless a link is given -- and this connector always sends one, so it is required here.

config.label: Link
config.description: A URL to attach. Facebook fetches and renders its own preview, so the title and image come from the page's OpenGraph tags rather than from anything sent here.

config.label: Publish immediately
config.description: Turn this off to create the post UNPUBLISHED, visible only to Page admins. Useful for review before it goes out.

outputShape.description: The post id, in the form `{page-id}_{post-id}`. Both halves are needed to address the post again -- the second half alone is not a valid id.
